why_this_file_exists: ADR-15's evidence standard: the bar is written and committed BEFORE the probe runs, so a result cannot be relabelled into a pass. This file is never amended; if the run reveals an outcome worth adding, it goes in a cycle-2 file that ADDS rather than rewrites, and the bar is the union.
webkit: expected to be unmeasurable on this host (ADR-10's recorded gap); the run records the launch failure verbatim rather than omitting the engine.

groups.M: Mechanism. A synthetic two-element pair (probe-tag) under full control of specificity, importance and stylesheet order, versus its flattened static twin. Establishes what the cross-sheet ::part() cascade actually is, independent of any shipped component.
groups.P: Reachability of a part nested one level deeper - the shipped sk-metric shape, where <sk-pill-tag> lives inside sk-metric's shadow root and no exportparts forwards its parts to the document.
groups.S: Shipped-surface value equality. Real sk-metric + sk-pill-tag elements and their real built sheets, resolved through the package export map, versus the naive static rewrite of sk-metric.css:67.
groups.H: ADR-15 follow-on. Whether the two-element wrapper ADR-15 rules for construct kinds 1 and 2 reproduces :host's CASCADE POSITION against a consumer's own rule, as distinct from its layout.

outcomes.state: shadow; reaching rule .wrap probe-tag::part(tag) (0,1,2); inner .tag (0,1,0); both set white-space
outcomes.expected: the OUTER (reaching) declaration applies

outcomes.state: shadow; reaching rule probe-tag::part(tag) at MINIMAL specificity (0,0,2); inner rule #probe.a.b.tag at (1,3,0)
outcomes.expected: the OUTER declaration still applies - specificity is not consulted across trees

outcomes.state: static twin of M2; reaching rewrite .wrap .tag (0,2,0); inner rewrite #probe.a.b.tag (1,3,0)
outcomes.expected: the INNER declaration applies - divergence from M2 is the outcome under test

outcomes.state: shadow; reaching sheet inserted BEFORE the element's own sheet is adopted
outcomes.expected: same as M1 - stylesheet order is not consulted across trees

outcomes.state: static twin; reaching rewrite and inner rule at EQUAL specificity (0,1,0) each, reaching rewrite ordered FIRST
outcomes.expected: the INNER (later) declaration applies - order decides where tree order used to

outcomes.state: shadow; inner declaration !important, reaching declaration normal
outcomes.expected: the INNER declaration applies (ordinary importance)

outcomes.state: shadow; BOTH declarations !important
outcomes.expected: the INNER declaration applies - importance REVERSES tree order

outcomes.state: static twin of M7; both !important, reaching rewrite at strictly higher specificity
outcomes.expected: the OUTER/reaching declaration applies - divergence from M7 is the outcome under test

outcomes.state: shadow; a PAGE rule .tag { letter-spacing: 9px } in a document stylesheet
outcomes.expected: no effect - a document class selector cannot match inside a shadow tree

outcomes.state: static twin of M9; the same page rule, page sheet ordered last, tie at (0,1,0)
outcomes.expected: 9px - divergence from M9 is the outcome under test

outcomes.state: real <sk-metric annotation>; document rule sk-pill-tag::part(tag) { letter-spacing: 9px }
outcomes.measures: letter-spacing on the pill's tag node inside sk-metric's shadow root
outcomes.expected: no effect - the pill is inside sk-metric's shadow root and ::part() reaches only one tree level

outcomes.state: real <sk-metric annotation>; document rule sk-metric::part(tag) { letter-spacing: 9px }
outcomes.measures: letter-spacing on the pill's tag node
outcomes.expected: no effect - sk-metric forwards no exportparts

outcomes.state: static twin; the same intent rewritten .sk-pill-tag { letter-spacing: 9px }, page sheet last
outcomes.measures: letter-spacing on the twin tag node
outcomes.expected: 9px - divergence from P1/P2 is the outcome under test

outcomes.state: real <sk-metric annotation>; document rule .sk-pill-tag { background: rgb(255,0,0) }
outcomes.measures: background-color on the pill's tag node
outcomes.expected: no effect - the pill's root is not reachable from the document at all

outcomes.state: static twin of P4, page sheet last
outcomes.measures: background-color on the twin tag node
outcomes.expected: rgb(255,0,0) - divergence from P4 is the outcome under test

outcomes.state: as S1 but with one additional inner-sheet rule at (0,2,0) setting white-space: nowrap, standing in for a variant compound the component owner may add at any time
outcomes.expected: shadow unchanged (normal); static twin flips to nowrap - divergence, and the component owner never touched sk-metric.css

outcomes.state: real <sk-action-row>; document rule sk-action-row { display: flex } at (0,0,1) against :host { display: block }
outcomes.expected: flex - a document rule beats :host regardless of specificity

outcomes.state: ADR-15's static wrapper .sk-action-row-host carrying the complete :host set; document rule div { display: flex } at (0,0,1)
outcomes.expected: block - the wrapper CLASS outbids the consumer's type selector; divergence from H1 is the outcome under test

outcomes.state: real <sk-action-row>; document rule sk-action-row { container-type: normal }
outcomes.measures: container-type on the host, and flex-wrap on .sk-action-row at a 360px width
outcomes.expected: the container is destroyed and @container (max-width:400px) stops firing - a consumer can switch the container off from the document

outcomes.state: ADR-15's static wrapper; document rule .sk-action-row-host { container-type: normal } at EQUAL specificity, page sheet ordered FIRST
outcomes.measures: container-type on the wrapper, and flex-wrap at 360px
outcomes.expected: the container SURVIVES - the library's rule is later, so the same consumer intent fails; divergence from H3 is the outcome under test
